Joy-Con 2 Dongle Tool

Flash the dongle firmware to an ESP32-S3 N16R8, then capture its log while you test. Works in Chrome, Edge or Opera on a desktop computer.

This browser can't reach USB serial ports. Open this file in Chrome, Edge or Opera on Windows, macOS, Linux or ChromeOS. If it still says this, serve the file locally (for example python -m http.server in its folder) and open http://localhost:8000.

  1. 1

    Put the board in download mode

    Hold BOOT, plug the board's USB (OTG) port into this computer, then release BOOT. Using the board's UART/COM port instead works without BOOT.

  2. 2

    Connect

    Pick the board in the browser's port list. In download mode it shows up as USB JTAG/serial debug unit (or as the UART chip's name).

    Loading flasher library…
  3. 3

    Flash

    Takes about 15 seconds at 921600 baud. Don't unplug the board until it says done.

Options
Also forgets every paired controller. Adds about 20 seconds.
Only matters on the UART/COM port; the USB port always runs at full speed.
For later builds. A -merged.bin goes at 0x0; the plain app image joycon2_dongle.bin goes at 0x10000. 

  


  


  

    

      
Connect to the dongle's log

      
Plug the dongle in normally, without BOOT, and pick its port:

      
    
        
  • Joy-Con 2 Dongle (dev): the normal firmware's log port.
    • 
        
  • USB JTAG/serial debug unit: the chip's built-in port. Use this with the diagnostic firmware, or to watch start-up.
    • 
        
  • UART/COM (second USB-C port, if your board has one): always carries the full log.
    •

Step 1 tests

      
Press Start on a test before doing it, so the log is labelled. Pick the result, add a note if anything was off, then save the report.
